summary: Malheur NF pole lookout in Grant County: dated notices put work in 1932-1935; the register says 1941; removed or destroyed in 1964.

facts.design: Pole L-4 lookout tower with a cab; a wood frame garage was erected in 1934
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1964; no source read describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Malheur National Forest

events.note: Item dated July 29, 1932, credited to the John Day Valley Ranger, says two men would start work on the lookout station (start of work, not completion)
Aladdin plan 16 by 18 foot wood frame garage erected
T-20 native timber tower with a 14 by 14 Aladdin Jr. cab completed, built by CCC crews
Earl Thompson at the lookout station (item quoted on Oregon Lookouts page)
Loren Dunten and his wife at the station (Burns Times-Herald item)
Old tower described as having been 'stubbed'; the page does not explain the word
New native wood tower placed under an existing house (Malheur Historical Record)
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: Item dated July 29, 1932, credited to the John Day Valley Ranger: two men to start work on the station; Malheur NF, Grant County
evidence.quote: July 29, 1932: "On Monday Leo Hardy and Herman Smith will start work on a lookout station at Wolf Mountain." (John Day Valley Ranger)

evidence.supports: About nine miles east-northeast of Silvies

evidence.quote: An Aladdin plan 16 by 18 foot wood frame garage was erected.
A plan T-20 native timber tower with a 14 by 14 Aladdin Jr. plan lookout cab was completed. Construction work performed by members of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: Register: built 1941, 30-foot pole L-4 tower, removed 1964
evidence.quote: Built in 1941, this 30' pole L-4 tower was removed in 1964.

evidence.supports: Earl Thompson at his lookout station, 1936
evidence.quote: Earl Thompson came in Monday afternoon from his forest lookout station on Wolf mountain

evidence.supports: Loren Dunten and wife came down from the station for a few hours and returned the next day, 1941
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Loren Dunten came down from Wolf Mountain Lookout Station Monday evening as it rained and they could get away for a few hours. They returned to the station Tuesday.

evidence.supports: New native wood tower placed under existing house, 1953
evidence.quote: New native wood tower placed under existing house

evidence.supports: Register's only recent picture is a 2002 photo of the site
evidence.quote: Wolf Mountain Lookout site 2002 - courtesy of Howard Verschoor

evidence.supports: Site is in the Malheur National Forest; administered by the Forest Service

corrections.why: The register gives a 30-foot pole tower (about 9.1 m) and firelookout.com gives 20 feet (about 6.1 m). The record's 5.5 m matches neither source. A reviewer should choose the value.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1941, but dated entries on the Oregon Lookouts page show work set to start in 1932 and a tower completed in 1935, with staffing in 1936 and 1941. The story gives the dated entries and reports the register's date as a disagreement.

sources.title: Wolf Mountain Lookout Site-MNF
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: register 1941 build versus dated entries 1932-1935. Height conflicts: 30 ft (register), 20 ft (firelookout.com); the record's 5.5 m matches neither. Removal conflicts: removed (register) versus destroyed (firelookout.com), both 1964. Geocache GC5B5BG (about this site) came up in search with a snippet mentioning footings, but the cached page is a stub, so it is not used; check it for what remains. The record's other_names 'Wolf Mountain' also fits two other Oregon lookouts (us-or-wolf-mountain, Wheeler County, standing; us-or-wolf-mountain-2, Lane County), so consider removing it. No source read gives an access level, so none is set.
